verdict.reasoning: Tried to refute on all four grounds and failed on each. (1) NOT reflow/absent-text: all seven headings are present in the markdown slice with correct numbers and correct titles, so nothing is literally missing — but the claim is about RANK, and the rank mismatch is exactly as stated. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 48225/48234 carry '### D.31.3.1 General' and '### D.31.3.2 CURRENT-DATE function'; lines 48255/48260/48265/48270/48275/48280/48285 carry '## D.31.3.3' … '## D.31.3.9'. Their own parent at line 48222 is '## D.31.3 Basic date and time intrinsic functions' — so the seven are emitted at the SAME markdown level as the clause that contains them. (2) NOT a misquote of the PDF: I read the 300-dpi render of page 1195 and pulled the PDF text layer with PyMuPDF. Every heading on 1195 (y=153.4, 229.3, 317.8, 393.7, 469.6, 545.4, 633.9) is Cambria,Bold 11.67 at x=80.0; D.31.3.1 (page 1194, y=343.1) and D.31.3.2 (y=469.6) are Cambria,Bold 11.67 at x=63.5, and the 80.0-vs-63.5 delta is only the recto/verso margin (page 1193 headings are also x=80.0). The obfuscated glyph runs confirm the depth: D.31.3 renders as 'D' + 5 masked chars ('.31.3'), while D.31.3.1 and every heading on 1195 render as 'D' + 7 masked chars ('.31.3.N'). ISO applies NO typographic rank distinction at this depth — D.31.3 itself is set in the identical Cambria,Bold 11.67 — so hierarchy is carried by the section NUMBER alone, and D.31.3.3 is unambiguously a depth-4 child of D.31.3, peer to D.31.3.1. (3) NOT page-break furniture or formatting: the page break is the CAUSE, not the substance. Markdown heading level is the transcription's machine-readable encoding of the section tree, not cosmetics; any TOC/outline/rule-catalog walker keyed on heading depth places D.31.3.3–.9 as siblings of D.31.3 rather than children, which is precisely the class of defect this reconciliation exists to catch (the page_workunit.py docstring records four rule-catalog extractor bugs already traced to transcription artefacts, one of them 'a heading demoted to bold'). (4) The meaning DOES change: the document tree asserts that D.31.3 contains two subclauses when the PDF prints nine. Mitigating detail: the HTML anchors are correct ('section-d-31-3-3' … 'section-d-31-3-9'), so anchor-based citation lookups still resolve; only level-based traversal is corrupted.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but mis-titled and under-scoped. Correct kind is wrong-heading-level (or heading-rank), NOT missing-heading: none of the seven headings is missing — all of D.31.3.3 through D.31.3.9 are present on page 1195 with correct numbers, correct titles, and correct anchors. The defect is that they are emitted at '##' while their same-depth peers D.31.3.1/D.31.3.2 are '###' and their own parent D.31.3 is also '##', collapsing seven children into siblings of their container. Scope is wider than page 1195: the identical artifact hits D.31.2.6 and D.31.2.7 ('##' at depth 4, across the 1193→1194 boundary) and D.31.5.2 through D.31.5.11 ('##' at depth 4, from the 1196→1197 boundary onward), and the depth-3 clauses D.31.2/D.31.3/D.31.4/D.31.5 are all '##' while their peer D.31.1 is '###'. The fix is therefore a level sweep over the whole of clause D.31 driven by the section number's dot-depth, not a seven-line patch to page 1195. PDF evidence for the equal-rank premise: every heading on pages 1193–1196, including D.31.3 itself, is Cambria,Bold 11.67 at the page's body indent, so the PDF encodes hierarchy solely in the section number.
